questions.question: What is the name of the SpaceX mission that launched a private astronaut crew to orbit Earth from pole to pole?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fram2.**__

• **SpaceX launched a private astronaut crew on the Fram2 mission, a unique polar-orbiting mission.**

__
 
• **The mission, named Fram2, was led by Chun Wang, a Maltese investor and cryptocurrency entrepreneur.**

• **During the mission, the astronauts participated in 22 research experiments focused on the effects of spaceflight on the human body.**

questions.question: Where is Project SeaCURE being piloted?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Weymouth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• SeaCURE – the first marine carbon capture system in Europe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Project SeaCURE** is a **UK-based pilot project** for carbon capture.

 
 
• 
 
It aims to **extract CO₂ directly from seawater**, enhancing the ocean's **natural carbon absorption** capacity.

 
 
• 
 
The project is being conducted in **Weymouth**, UK.

 
 
• 
 
**Funded by the UK government**, it explores a **cost-effective, scalable** method to reduce **atmospheric CO₂**.

 
 
• 
 
It differs from traditional methods which capture CO₂ **from emissions or directly from the air**.

 
 
• 
 
Oceans hold **up to 150 times more carbon** than the atmosphere.

 
 
• 
 
SeaCURE uses **sustainable materials** for its operations.

 
 
• 
 
The goal is to **capture CO₂ before it escapes into the atmosphere**, helping to **combat climate change**.

questions.question: When is Prevention of Blindness Week observed in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**April 1 to April 7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Prevention Of Blindness Week: 1-7 April.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Prevention of Blindness Week** is observed in India from **April 1 to April 7** every year to raise awareness about blindness prevention and encourage eye check-ups.

 
 
• 
 
The initiative is in collaboration with organizations like **Sight Savers** and **Rotary International**.

 
 
• 
 
India is often referred to as the **"blind capital of the world** due to the high number of people with visual impairments.

 
 
• 
 
India was the **first country** to seek a subsidized loan from the **World Bank’s International Development Agency** to address blindness.

 
 
• 
 
The week promotes **routine eye check-ups** and the adoption of **healthy habits** for vision care.

 
 
• The National Society for the Prevention of Blindness was founded in 1960 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Raj Kumari Amrit Kaur under the Societies Registration Act of 1860.

The Central Government provides approximately **26 lakh metric tonnes** of foodgrains through the **Food Corporation of India (FCI)**.

 
 
• 
 
The government bears **100% cost** of foodgrains, including:

 
 
• 
 
A subsidy of about **9,000 crore rupees** per annum.

 
 
• 
 
**100% transportation cost** of foodgrains from FCI depots to schools.

questions.question: How many moons does Saturn now have, making it the planet with the most moons in the Solar System?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**274**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• Saturn has “gained” 128 new moons in a groundbreaking discovery by astronomers in Taiwan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• 
 
**Saturn’s new title:** "Moon Champion" with 274 moons.

 
 
• 
 
**Discovery significance:** Saturn surpasses all other planets combined in number of moons.

 
 
• 
 
**Moons discovered:** 128 new moons, primarily small (a few kilometers in size).

 
 
• 
 
**Type of moons:** Irregular moons with elliptical orbits at various angles.

 
 
• 
 
**Formation of irregular moons:** Likely small planets captured by Saturn’s gravity and shattered by collisions.

 
 
• 
 
**Insights into Saturn’s rings:** Irregular moons provide clues about Saturn's rings, which are believed to be fragments from comets, asteroids, and moons torn apart by Saturn’s gravity.

 
 
• 
 
**Naming convention:** Moons are temporarily designated with technical names (e.g., "S/2020 S 27") and await official names from the International Astronomical Union (IAU).

 
 
• 
 
**Saturn's Rings:** Composed mainly of water ice with a minor amount of rocky material.

 
 
• 
 
**Titan:** Largest moon of Saturn, even larger than Mercury and Pluto.
